rationale: M60.P1. This lane's documentation claimed `parameters`, `returnType` and `decorators` on C++ symbols while the M60 payload-seam matrix recorded all three as DEAD emit cells — the doc described a payload the analyzer never produced. The pins below are written from the MEASURED GRAMMAR SHAPES (dumped from the tree-sitter AST, quoted in the comments on each pin) and from C++ semantics, not scraped from analyzer output; they were then confirmed against it. Two of them are the strongest kind of pin here, because they fail on a REVERT rather than on a missing feature: (1) the parameter TYPE slice is taken at the NAME node, so `const std::string& name` pins as `const std::string&` — the pre-fix slice stopped at the declarator, whose text is `& name`, and published `const std::string`, a different C++ type that overloads differently; (2) a defaulted parameter is a distinct `optional_parameter_declaration` node, so `scale` is pinned at all, and skipping that node type loses every defaulted parameter in the corpus. `forbidParameters.types` pins the same slice from the negative side — the parameter's own NAME must never appear in its TYPE field, the last-resort-scan failure shape the csharp lane registered for exactly this reason.

expectParameters.comment: a constructor is NORMALIZED to the name `constructor`; ownerName is the only way to address one, which is why the decorator matcher needs it too

forbidParameters.comment: the variadic ellipsis is not in configure
a `...` has no name and no type; publishing it would put a name in the family parameter shape that a consumer cannot resolve
the parameter's own NAME must never appear in its TYPE field — the last-resort-type-scan failure shape (csharp lane R7)

expectDecorators.comment: a method's trailing `const` is a child of its function_declarator, NOT of the declaration — a declaration-only scan publishes [] here, and `const` is on essentially every getter in the corpus

forbidDecorators.comment: `Point` is a plain struct: no modifier on it may be invented from its members'
configure overrides nothing; the field must not absorb a sibling's modifier
